Operation

Site masking

Exclude genomic regions whose variation would mislead downstream comparison.

Inputs

  • Reference genome

Outputs

  • Mask coordinates (BED)

Some regions produce variation that does not reflect shared ancestry or cannot be measured reliably. Masking them keeps them from inflating distances or distorting trees. Coordinates are defined on the reference so they apply identically to every sample. When more than one masking method is used, their regions are merged into a single mask.

Choosing methods 3

These methods address different problems and can be combined. Apply each one whose conditions match your data.

  • Custom masking

    Mask regions you define yourself in a BED file, such as genes known to be unreliable for your species.

    Use when

    • Published analyses of your species exclude specific genes or regions, such as PE/PPE genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
    • Your own data show regions with consistently poor coverage, mapping quality, or excess variant calls.
    • You need to reproduce another lab's analysis exactly, using the same mask they used.

    Skip this method when

    • The regions can be found reproducibly with a prediction tool, which is easier to rerun when the reference changes.

    Combine with

    • Mobile element masking: Use both when you have species-specific regions in addition to predicted mobile elements.
    • Repeat and paralog masking: Use both when you have species-specific regions in addition to repeats found by self-alignment.

    BEDTools

  • Mobile element masking

    Mask prophages, insertion sequences, and other mobile elements in a bacterial reference.

    Use when

    • The organism is a bacterium whose genomes carry prophages, insertion sequences, or other horizontally acquired elements.
    • You want SNP distances and trees to reflect the chromosome's clonal history.

    Combine with

    • Repeat and paralog masking: Add it when the reference also contains repeats such as rRNA operons or duplicated genes, which cause ambiguous read mapping.
    • Custom masking: Add your own BED file for species-specific regions that prediction tools do not find.

    PHASTEST · ISEScan

  • Repeat and paralog masking

    Mask repetitive and duplicated regions of a reference so reads cannot map ambiguously.

    Use when

    • The genome contains gene families, duplicated genes, or other repeats, as is common in fungi.
    • Variant calls cluster in regions with unusually high or uneven coverage.

    Combine with

    • Mobile element masking: Add it for bacteria, whose horizontally transferred elements are not necessarily repeated in the reference.
    • Custom masking: Add your own BED file for species-specific regions that prediction tools do not find.

    MUMmer (nucmer self-alignment) · RepeatMasker
